claims.statement: Buffer, Inc. provides social publishing, scheduling and analytics; legal contact is in San Francisco, while origin was Birmingham, UK and operations are now distributed.
Joel Gascoigne is founder/CEO; Leo Widrich joined the early business and marketing. By May 2011 both had left other paid work to focus on Buffer.
Pricing and recruiting pages were accessible during this research. Company is operating as of observation; no acquisition or shutdown established.

Joel built the initial scheduler during evenings/weekends over seven weeks, shared an interest/pricing page on Twitter and launched on 2010-11-30 with Hacker News feedback. He describes an earlier product with insufficient customer conversations.
First paying customer arrived within four days of launch; early payment was $5. Roughly 100 early signups were not 100 paying customers. By May 2011 revenue was roughly $1,000/month.
Leo pitched guest articles to bloggers; founder reports roughly 20% acceptance. Guest blogging contributed to early 100,000 users; neither paid-user counts nor causal attribution are established.
2012 account describes rejected press pitches, blog repositioning, about 150 external guest articles and Lifehacker syndication. These are historical tactics, not a claim of fraud.

2025 growth operator reports organic search, direct, LLM referrals and paid acquisition; focus was signup-to-activation-to-paid conversion plus lifecycle communication. Budget was unchanged YoY and marketing team under ten. No percentage channel mix disclosed.

Paid plans charge by social channel, with annual and monthly billing. Trial lasts 14 days; without payment details users revert to Free. Channel removal is possible: indefinite captivity is not established.
Published history records $5/month entry in 2010, $10 in 2012, $15 in 2017, and per-channel pricing from 2021. These historical tiers are not current offers.
WebFX social-media manager Katie Goodling describes replacing centralized manual CSV handling with drafts, scheduling and client approvals. Vendor case study reports 40 hours saved monthly.

Disclosed financing: $120k AngelPad in August 2011, $330k seed in December 2011, $3.5M Series A in December 2014. Of Series A, $2.5M was liquidity for founders and early team, not all primary company cash.
In July 2018 Buffer spent $3.3M buying out seven Series A investors whose original investment was $2.3M. This was a shareholder buyback, not sale of the business.

June 2016 report describes ten layoffs (11% of team) following overhiring/cash problems. Content Suggestions and Daily experiments were stopped; reported expected savings about $100k/month were not measured realized profit.
Current policy is four workdays with a flexible meeting-free fifth day. Historical 2015 hours survey was only eleven participants; neither source establishes current founder weekly hours.
2021 support account describes staggered days off, weekend coverage and dedicated advocates aiming at seven-day service. It does not establish current ticket volume, exact hours or outsourcing spend.

Recruitment description reports React/TypeScript, Radix-based Popcorn UI, GraphQL/Apollo, Node/TypeScript, MongoDB and AWS/Kubernetes. A separate infrastructure role lists GCP, Cloudflare, Terraform, EKS, Helm, ArgoCD, GitHub Actions, Redis and monitoring services.

Legal page names AWS, Anthropic, Cloudflare, MongoDB Atlas, OpenAI, Stripe, Help Scout, Customer.io, ChartMogul and Xero among subprocessors. Listing establishes declared relationships, not monthly spend or exact AI models.

Terms/privacy/DPA describe personal-data processing, intellectual-property procedures and third-party service conditions. Platform and contractual obligations apply; no claim of zero legal/payment-provider risk is made.

From August 2025 reporting, cancellation is recognized immediately rather than after the prepaid period. July removed over 1,300 inactive legacy annual subscriptions. Pre/post MRR and ARR comparisons require this basis change.
Bulk upload supports up to 100 posts from CSV in the August 2025 report. Staff AI allowance announced in February 2025 was a productivity budget, not evidence of full automation.

Sprout Social and Hootsuite are direct comparison targets; manual native posting/CSV are substitutes. Sprout's own page offers Essentials, so a claim that enterprise competitors cannot serve small users is unsupported.
2025 net income and the profit-share pool are reported in the 2026-02-04 article. Individual founder distributions, taxes and net personal bank receipts are not disclosed.

derived.text: 投稿の手作業を月額課金に変えたBuffer。2025年の会社純利益は約251万ドル。個人の手残りや完全自動の稼ぎではない。
作ったのに需要を確かめきれなかった前作の経験から、Joelは自身が困った投稿予約を絞って作った。創業者の内面や資産状況は推測しない。
SNSごと・時刻ごとの投稿と承認作業を、まとめて処理する道具に変えた。価格の対象は投稿文章そのものより、運用担当者の反復作業。
最初はTwitterとHNで公開し早期に有料客を得た。その後は外部ブログへの寄稿で既存読者へ接触。単発の裏技だけで現在の規模になったわけではない。
無料で試し、チャネル追加・分析・チーム承認で継続課金。繰り返す運用を課金点にする一方、人員・サポート・外部APIが費用と制約として残る。
代理店担当者が買うのは、投稿漏れ・確認往復・CSV整形に時間を奪われない状態。顧客の恐怖や羞恥を本人確認済みの心理としては扱わない。
蓄積した運用手順と承認フロー、複数SNS連携が継続利用の理由になり得る。データ監禁や解約不能の証明はない。
投稿先プラットフォームの変更、検索流入の変動、採用費膨張が利益を削る。過去の赤字と競合の低価格参入は、永続的高利益を否定する反証。
2025年は流入量の拡大だけでなく登録後の転換改善が伸びを支えたという報告。AI流入・複数SNS運用の変化は観測対象だが、2026年の新規参入者の収益を保証しない。
狙いの候補は特定業種の承認・投稿・報告の往復作業。ただし未充足市場であること、獲得費、再現利益は未検証。一般的な予約投稿のコピーだけでは既存各社と競合する。
年額の前受けは現金回収を早め得るが、継続サービス義務を伴う。入金と売上・純利益は別。外部資金を使っていない事業という説明も過去の調達に反する。
小口チャネル課金と席単位課金には客層・価格差がある。ただしSproutもEssentialsを提供しており、大手が小口を売れないという断定は成立しない。
